<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="choose-a-direction"><a href="#choose-a-direction">Choose a direction</a></h2>

Start with the problem you want to understand. ABI is the runtime and orchestration project. WDBX is semantic storage associated with ABI. Abbey is the companion identity and interaction direction. Gama is a separate Swift application-framework project.

The guides connect those roles without pretending that a conceptual map is a production deployment. Choose a project, read its scope, then inspect the source instructions for the revision you intend to use.

- New to the ecosystem? Read Getting started.
- Evaluating a capability? Read Evidence and limitations.
- Working in the existing website? Read Platform and site architecture.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="read-the-evidence"><a href="#read-the-evidence">Read the evidence</a></h2>

A source description tells you what the project documents. Reported test coverage tells you what its authors say the tests cover. A measured result needs a specific artifact, method, environment, date, and revision. These are different kinds of evidence.

This preview does not execute ABI, run a model, or open a WDBX store. It publishes no measured performance claims. Source references below identify what was reviewed and what is simply an upstream reference.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="use-the-guides"><a href="#use-the-guides">Use the guides</a></h2>

Search with the documentation search control or Control/Command + K. Search runs against the articles bundled with this site; it is not an AI answer service and does not send the query to a server.

Each guide has stable headings, source references, and adjacent-page navigation. The copy controls copy documentation, not the result of a command run. Follow upstream prerequisites before executing anything in your own checkout.

</section>
